title: Rational smooth purity naturality and Frobenius mate identification
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], with $\ell\ne p$ and $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$ in its rational/common-stage constructible categories. Let $X_0,Y_0$ be separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes and $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ a separated finite-type $k_0$-morphism. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $f=f_0\times_{k_0}k$, and assume $f$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $g_X,g_Y$ be their geometric-Frobenius automorphisms and $P_X=Lg_X^*$, $P_Y=Lg_Y^*$ [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Write $F=Rf_!$ and $G=Rf^!$ for the constructible adjoint pair of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], with $F$ computed from a compactification $c=(j,\bar f)$ of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] that is the base change to $k$ of a compactification of $f_0$. Use the previously specified canonical purity maps $\gamma_{f,K}:H(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(K)$ of [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity], with $H(K)=Lf^*K(d)[2d]$, transporting the finite canonical maps [def-pur-smooth-purity-map].

For every morphism $u:K\to L$ in $D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, under the canonical pullback, twist and shift identifications,
$$G(u)\circ\gamma_{f,K}=\gamma_{f,L}\circ H(u).$$
Let $b_K:P_XH(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(P_YK)$ be pullback composition for $fg_X=g_Yf$, followed by the tensor, shift and canonical Tate-line comparison $P_X\Lambda_X(d)\simeq\Lambda_X(d)$ of [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. Let $\beta:P_YF\xrightarrow{\sim}FP_X$ be the canonical compact-support exchange for that Cartesian square, formed with $c$ and its pullback along $g_Y$. Then
$$e_K=\gamma_{f,P_YK}\circ b_K\circ(P_X\gamma_{f,K})^{-1}:P_XG(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(P_YK)$$
is the right adjunction mate of $\beta^{-1}:FP_X\to P_YF$ under $F\dashv G$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; equivalently, with counit $\varepsilon:FG\to\mathrm{id}$,
$$\varepsilon_{P_YK}\circ F(e_K)=P_Y(\varepsilon_K)\circ\beta_{G(K)}^{-1}.$$
Both assertions are identities in the rational category and, for $\Qlb$, in the common-stage category. In particular naturality applies to every rational Weil isomorphism $P_YK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, without requiring a Frobenius-stable integral lattice.

source.place: Proof sentence 3 (geometric orientation and trace) and sentence 4 (formal duality exchange from evaluation and adjunction maps)

proof.text: All schemes in the statement are separated finite type over $k$. They are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (a field is Noetherian), and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; $\ell$ is invertible since $\ell\ne p$. Thus they satisfy the scheme hypotheses of the integral and rational categories. By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] an $E$-object is an integral object viewed in a scalar localization; this choice of an underlying integral object does not equip it with an integral Weil structure.

source.place: Proof sentences 3–4, expanded rational naturality and adjunction argument

proof.text: Identify the integral presentation of Step 1 with [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. For such an integral constructible object $K$, [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] gives a single Tor-amplitude interval for all its derived reductions; hence its reduction tower lies in the domain of [det-sp-tower-gamma]. The powers $\ell^n$ used there are a cofinal subsystem of uniformizer powers: in the DVR $\ell$ is a unit times $\varpi_E^{e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)}$, so $\mathcal O_E/(\ell^n)=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^{en})$. No additional finite-Tor condition on a rational object is being imposed.

source.place: Proof sentences 3–4, expanded rational naturality and adjunction argument

proof.text: Apply the naturality assertion in clause (2) of [det-sp-tower-gamma] to the actual derived reduction of an integral arrow $v:K\to L$. Apply the functor $R\varprojlim$ to that equality. The natural Hom bijections and purity formula of [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection] identify the result with $G(v)\gamma_K=\gamma_LH(v)$ for the integral purity maps. Identify its right adjoint $H_{f,\mathcal O_E}$ with the specified $Rf^!$ using their constructible adjunctions [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the unique counit-preserving natural isomorphism [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. This fixes the adjunction normalization used below.

source.place: Proof sentences 3–4, expanded rational naturality and adjunction argument

proof.text: The square with horizontal arrows $g_X,g_Y$ is Cartesian as a square of schemes by [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]. To apply a theorem stated for $k$-morphisms, give its source copy of each $T=X,Y$ the structure map $a_Tg_T=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)a_T$; call it $T^{\langle\gamma\rangle}$. Then $g_T:T^{\langle\gamma\rangle}\to T$ is a $k$-isomorphism, and the left vertical arrow is the same underlying $f$, now $f^{\langle\gamma\rangle}$. The source schemes remain separated finite type and this arrow remains smooth of dimension $d$, since these changes compose structural maps with a field isomorphism. The canonical twist comparison for this square is precisely the roots-of-unity pullback comparison specified in [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. In particular the square does not replace geometric Frobenius by a $k$-linear absolute-Frobenius endomorphism.

source.place: Proof sentences 3–4, expanded rational naturality and adjunction argument

proof.text:
Choose the compactification $c$ of the statement as follows. Since $Y_0$ is of finite type over a field it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so [thm-nagata-compactification] gives a compactification $X_0\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X_0\xrightarrow{\bar f_0}Y_0$ of the separated finite-type $f_0$; its base change $c=(j,\bar f)$ to $k$ is a compactification of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], by base change of open immersions and proper morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. By [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian] for $\bar f_0$, the square $\bar fg_{\overline X}=g_Y\bar f$ is Cartesian, and $jg_X=g_{\overline X}j$ since both are base changes of $j_0$. Hence the pullback of $c$ along $g_Y$, used by [det-sp-tower-exceptional-bc], is identified by $g_{\overline X}$ with the same underlying compactification $(j,\bar f)$ of the retagged $f^{\langle\gamma\rangle}$, which is the compactification used in [lem-pur-tower-purity-ground-field-retagging]. Work first in the ordinary derived category of coefficient towers, retaining its transition maps. Apply [det-sp-purity-bc-factors] to the retagged $k$-Cartesian square of Step 4. Its $e_\bullet$ is the transpose of inverse compact-support exchange by [det-sp-tower-exceptional-bc], not merely an isomorphism with the same endpoints. Its conclusion is
$$e_{\bullet,K}\,P_X\gamma_{\bullet,K}=\gamma_{f^{\langle\gamma\rangle},\bullet,P_YK}\,b_{\bullet,K}.$$
By [lem-pur-tower-purity-ground-field-retagging], identify the retagged purity on the right with $\gamma_{f,\bullet,P_YK}$, using the identity of the underlying sites, the same compactification, and the counit-preserving right-adjoint comparison. Multiplying on the right by $(P_X\gamma_{\bullet,K})^{-1}$ proves the displayed purity formula for the actual tower mate. This is an equality in the derived category of towers, not a conclusion from equality of its separate evaluations.

source.place: Proof sentences 3–4, expanded rational naturality and adjunction argument

proof.text:
Realize the normalized towers of Step 5 in the integral category by [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. The pullback and compact-support identifications are the natural ones of [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower]. The compatibility with the actual compactification exchange, including its open/proper maps and units/counits before evaluation, is [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization], applied to the $k$-morphisms in the retagged square. The integral adjunction of [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection] has precisely the realized tower counit. Consequently applying this functor to the tower transpose equation gives
$$\varepsilon_{P_YK}F(e_K)=P_Y(\varepsilon_K)\beta_{GK}^{-1}$$
in the integral category. Applying it to the equality in Step 5 gives $e_K=\gamma_{P_YK}b_K(P_X\gamma_K)^{-1}$. The counit-preserving comparison in Step 3 identifies these with the specified $G$ and $\gamma$. These two conclusions use functorial realization of tower arrows; they do not use faithfulness of finite-level evaluation.

source.place: Proof sentences 3–4, expanded rational naturality and adjunction argument

proof.text: Keep the maps constructed in Steps 3–6 distinct from the already specified purity: denote the former by $\gamma^T$. Apply [lem-pur-tower-trace-purity-comparison] to $f$ with the same compactification, normalized reductions and counit-preserving right-adjoint comparison. Its integral comparison is $\gamma^{\mathrm{tr}}_{E,K}=\gamma^T_{E,K}$, where $\gamma^{\mathrm{tr}}$ uses any reconstructed unit orientation, its scalar-extended trace and the projection transpose. Its rational conclusion identifies the actual chosen maps of [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]: $\gamma^{\mathrm{rat}}_{f,Q_EK}=Q_E(\gamma^T_{E,K})$, with the stated coefficient comparisons. Hence the naturality and counit equations proved above for $\gamma^T$ apply to the intended family after localization. This uses a comparison of the unit orientation and of the actual transposes; equality of arbitrary coherent lifts is not assumed.

source.place: Proof sentences 3–4, expanded rational naturality and adjunction argument

proof.text:
Pass to $E$ by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport], using the rational operations on arrows of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the actual purity-family identification established in Step 7. For any rational arrow write $u=\varpi_E^{-N}v$ with $v$ integral, possible by [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Both $H_E$ and $G_E$ act by this scalar-extension rule. Thus Steps 3 and 7 give, in the localized Hom group,
$$G_E(u)\gamma_K=\varpi_E^{-N}G_E(v)\gamma_K=\varpi_E^{-N}\gamma_LH_E(v)=\gamma_LH_E(u).$$
This proves naturality for every rational arrow, whether or not it lifts to an integral isomorphism.

source.place: Proof sentences 3–4, expanded rational naturality and adjunction argument

proof.text: Apply the localization functor also to the two integral equations of Step 6. It preserves composites and inverses, so $e_E=\gamma_{P_YK}b_K(P_X\gamma_K)^{-1}$ and $\varepsilon_{P_YK}F_E(e_E)=P_Y(\varepsilon_K)\beta_{G_EK}^{-1}$ remain equalities. The rational adjunction is the one whose units and counits agree with this passage, by [lem-coef-rational-operations]. Take $L_1=L_2=F_E$, $R_1=R_2=G_E$, and the connecting functors $P_X,P_Y$ in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Its transpose characterization says exactly that the latter equation identifies $e_E$ with the mate of $\beta^{-1}:F_EP_X\to P_YF_E$. This checks the direction of the inverse exchange as well as the adjunction normalization.

source.place: Proof sentences 3–4, expanded rational naturality and adjunction argument

proof.text: For $\Qlb$, use the common-stage categories of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Clauses (2)–(3) of [det-sp-field-extension-towers] intertwine the actual tower purity, preserve its units and counits, and give coefficient-composition compatibility. Step 7 identifies its rational image with the intended purity, with precisely these coefficient comparisons. The adjunction identifications preserve units and counits under finite scalar extension by [lem-coef-rational-operations], and the actual rational compact-support exchange satisfies its scalar comparison equation by [lem-cbc-rational-compact-support-coefficient-coherence]. The pullback/twist comparisons and their action on common-stage arrows are those of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. Therefore the expressions in Steps 8–9 are compatible natural transformations and their equations descend by [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors]. Concretely, represent an arbitrary arrow $u$ over one common finite extension $M$, apply Step 8 at $M$, and conjugate the two sides by the same scalar comparison isomorphisms. For the mate equation take the representative at the stage of $K$ and apply Step 9. The resulting equalities of representatives give exactly the asserted equalities of morphism classes.

source.place: Proof sentences 3–4, expanded rational naturality and adjunction argument

proof.text:
Finally let $\theta:P_YK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ be any Weil structure in the category of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Apply Step 8 or 10 with $u=\theta$ and $K$ there replaced by $P_YK$: $G(\theta)\gamma_{P_YK}=\gamma_KH(\theta)$. Substitute the formula for $e_K$ and cancel $P_X\gamma_K$ to obtain
$$G(\theta)e_KP_X\gamma_K=\gamma_KH(\theta)b_K.$$
Thus the purity comparison intertwines the Weil structure made from the adjunction mate with the pullback/twist Weil structure. No step selected a lattice stable under $\theta$; the fraction calculation treated $\theta$ itself as an arbitrary rational arrow.
